tweets.text:
The best traders are very fluid

You could have had an idea yesterday, thats no longer valid today or whatever time frame. But ultimately, you aren't married to any idea or position. Whether you are trading eth, or wheat futures. All that matters is your pnl. They are really just tickers to trade with changing narratives, rotations, and liquidity. Sometimes people get on a trend late and still make more than someone who was early. People are wrong all the time, but the best learn to correct it quick and admit that. More often than not marrying a ticker comes with many big costs whether emotional, or financially. 

All that matters is what you make, and keep, and that we get paid for the risk we take. See so many people crap on people who had an idea one week, and then the opposite week their opinion changed as new information came in. That's exactly how you are suppose to be. fluid

$BTC There has been quite a bit of open interest ramp up over the past two days.

Well over $1.3B on Bitcoin alone has entered.

$BTC Has mirrored the 2023 price action extremely well.

I do still believe that if you were to see some bigger flush due to a headline or bond market breaking for example, that it would be an interesting spot to watch.

Will keep track on how the fractal evolves. Keep in mind, this is just a comparison. Different market, different times, but always interesting to compare similar price action.

quote.text:
bitcoin:native With the 2023 breakout from the bear market as overlay.

The price action at the bottom with the second sweep into very compressed sideways and the breakout has been very similar.

In 2023 at this point, a lot of people were calling for another lower low to occur. Sentiment was pretty neutral on average.

What actually happened was about 6 weeks of sideways chop. We saw some up and down and a larger correction during the banking crisis fud at the start of 2023. But that quickly reversed into a positive catalyst for Bitcoin instead and saw another leg up follow after that.

I think any larger drawdowns due to some kind of headline should be welcomed with open arms. Mark out your high timeframe levels and stay level headed. 

And remember that usually price tends to shake out a lot of positions on both sides before actually continuing its move higher after such a big impulse.

tweets.text:
Let's discuss luck a little bit. I consider myself, extremely lucky but luck is something you can create, and generate. 

There's several kinds of luck. There is luck from pure chance, where you did nothing to cause it. You were truly in the right place at the right time. This is the only one you can't control.

There is luck from motion, which come from opportunities you create by doing things. investing, trading, starting a business, meeting people, building things. Most of the time, it goes nowhere but you expose yourself to a larger surface area of luck which means more chances for something unexpected in a good way to happen. 

Luck from awareness. An opportunity presents itself for thousands of people to see. But you are one of the people capable of seeing it. This comes from years of experience that train you to see things most people overlook. This imo happens constantly in investing where the information and opportunity are public and you're able to recognize the significance of it. So the luck isnt finding the information instead its simply recognizing it. 

Then the last is luck unique to you. you have developed relationships, skills, or a unique brand. Someone like threadguy comes to mind here. You became the type of person or a person that lucky events can happen to.

So you have the ability to create 2-4, 1 is just by chance. But there is a saying that luck is the residue of hardwork. So essentially, lucky people just expose themselves to it more.  The people who succeed at the end of the day are the people who take chances. It doesnt mean they are guaranteed to succeed bc most people wont. but you certainly increase the odds of it

tweets.text:
The end and start of the month and quarter are usually choppy and love sweeping liquidity (on both sides).

Not the place where you want to position yourself directionally straight away usually.

Usually best to let it play out some days and then reassess.

quote.text:
$BTC The last and first week of the calendar month have been awful places to trade directionally. The past 4 months have only seen bad market environments in those weeks.

Pretty much all the action has come from the third week of the month. This usually comes after weak price action into that week only for it to reverse from there.

Of course the sample size is small but the main thing you should take away from this is that most action happens in a short timeframe. The market has been moving like this for years now.

Miss the few big moves and you need to be very patient again for the next one, both up and down.

Most of what this market has become is sideways for weeks or even months only for the actual action to occur in a short few day/week timeframe.

$BTC If this deviates below $83K I am going more defensive mode until the Fed/Treasury steps in and defends the long end yields in some shape or form like Bessent tried doing a month ago.

That didn't have any effect in the end for the yields but did spark the BTC & Crypto rally halfway through August.

Alternative could be Trump taco'ing on the war which should ease inflation expectations, bring oil down and also gets yields lower.

Midterms next month so maybe he'll time it right before so the "win", which he would label it as, is fresh in everyone's minds.

I think that if the chart confirms a breakdown after sweeping the may highs at $83K, with these things at play, it doesn't hurt just taking it chill until something changes

It has been an amazing few months for gains so rather defend that capital while it is still at its highs.

For now let's see if $83K holds or if the bulls can retake $85K. We've just been ranging here for the past week in the end.

But below $83K this will be my train of thought. I also think that would signal a more risk off environment for alts if it happens.

High timeframe market structure flips are great, but you do need to see follow through. A rejection below your breakout level as sentiment flips bullish and lots of ETF flows come in above, is not the recipe for the continuation of a bullish environment you want to see.

Just my two cents.

tweets.text:
Crypto launches have largely been PvP.

One trader’s exit is another trader’s loss.

But Ethereum hasn’t really had a DEX or launchpad capture attention in the past few years.

Interesting to see @motoswap testing a different model as activity starts coming back to Ethereum.

PvE, Player vs. Environment, is designed to align participants around growing the launch and its liquidity, rather than competing against each other.

Motoswap is now live, with traders also getting rakeback from the fees they generate.

Could be an interesting moment for Ethereum. Take a look, curious what people think.

quote.text:
We might not have seen a ton of crazy new technologies or sectors developed this past cycle, but we have seen a big move towards actual revenue generating companies.

Even the big DeFi protocols from the past few years are still raking in millions a month and have since also implemented some form of fee switch or buyback mechanism.

The 2021 cycle kind of felt like the dot com bubble for DeFi. A lot of hype, no sustainable revenue/value accrual for holders. Coins fell and many have not made it back to that top since.

With most investor unlocks done from protocols that did launch that cycle, I think at some point these can be pretty good long term spot buys. I don't think the likes of $UNI, $AAVE etc are going anywhere. But you might need a lot of patience for these and have a multi-year horizon.

Newer protocols like $ENA, $PUMP and of course $HYPE are interesting but will have more volatile revenue and still have token unlocks ahead, so timing will be more difficult. I think ENA & PUMP will perform incredible during a hot market, but that's the key.

Just some random thoughts. I think many of these big protocols have come down to reasonable levels by now. Obviously DeFi itself has not been hot while $ETH has underperformed this cycle too.

But I don't think the DeFi lull lasts forever.

tweets.text:
Do you trade with a large portfolio?

Then you know liquidity and execution quality matter.

The bigger the order, the more important things like order-book depth, spreads, slippage, and consistency of execution become.

TokenInsight’s latest report compares BTC & ETH spot liquidity across major exchanges, and the results are interesting.

Binance stands out for consistency, especially on ETH.

But I was positively surprised by MEXC. It performs strongly across both assets and records the lowest median BTC slippage at the $500K order size.

The bigger takeaway:

Trading volume alone doesn’t tell you how good an exchange’s liquidity really is.

For larger trades, what matters is how much depth is available, how tight the spread is, and how much price impact you actually get when executing size.

tweets.text:
$BTC looks like it’s forming a short-term bottom around the $84K area.

I could see one final push toward $88K before another leg lower into the low $80Ks.

If the downside continues, I’d be watching the 50W MA around $79K as a deeper support zone. 

The 50W MA is an important medium-to-long-term trend indicator and can act as support during larger pullbacks.

So the levels I’m watching:

$84K → short-term base

$88K → potential relief-rally resistance

Low $80Ks → next downside target

~$79K → 50W MA / deeper support

A short-term bounce doesn’t necessarily mean the broader correction is over.

tweets.text:
I know people have been making grave allegations against Loom lately, and I don’t know if they have merit.

But people massively underestimate the mental impact of having a phone in their hands or pocket on their ability to focus on the present moment. It goes far beyond cinema, gym, studying, meals, family time, sleep… Anything requiring attention.

This is not slop. Although the concept isn’t novel, such devices have the potential for a massive worldwide market and to change the world for the better. Phone addiction is a poison; look inside any city restaurant or public transport. People don’t enjoy each other’s presence and are more like walking zombies hypnotized by their phones.

I support the idea. Distribution and marketing are the key issues. People haven’t read the massive body of literature or lack the IQ to understand the stakes and applications.

This is the kind of step I like to see toward public understanding of how badly phones affect our relationships and health.

Disclaimer: I didn’t invest in LoomLock. I am fortunately not rekt by monetary controversies that may or may not be true (no clue). I just like what I see and feel it gets hated undeservedly.

tweets.text:
$BTC How quick things can change. Just over a month ago BTC was struggling in the low $60Ks as it was sitting at high timeframe support.

Now it has flipped all its weekly levels and any buys done last month are sitting very pretty.

That is why I always preach to stay level headed and don't count a level broken (both up and down) before it actually is broken.

A lot of people did not start buying in the months BTC spend in the $60Ks because the cycle "had to" bottom in October.

Meanwhile, price held its support and rallied almost 50% from its lows to the recent highs.

Averaging in low is always the way to do it. Even if you are not certain it is the final bottom yet.

For now, eyes on $83K to see if BTC can close the weekly above it and fully confirm the weekly market structure break.

quote.text:
$BTC Failing to push above the $65K mark.

Every attempt at doing so is being pushed back down. Stocks meanwhile at all time highs and crypto getting left behind again as has been the theme for a while now.

Just keep an eye on the high timeframe levels, there will be plenty of time to DCA or buy into momentum when the time is right.

Personally, I am still slowly accumulating spot but will keep dry powder on the side for if things turn worse over the next few months. Still doubt this will trade meaningfully below ~$40K or so which is about my lowest I'd see this go. Any black swan events aside.

So with that in mind, and my assumption that $BTC will head to $200K+ at some point, I already like my slow spot buys in this region.

It's just a matter of taking it slow until then.

My stock portfolio has been the savior in 2026 though, definitely happy to have some long term capital put aside there.

tweets.text:
RWA gets measured by how much value gets tokenized.

I think that’s the wrong metric.

Tokenizing the asset is becoming table stakes. Custodians can do it. Banks can do it. DTCC is about to do it at scale.

The harder question is what happens after the asset is tokenized.

Because an asset sitting onchain with no activity is just a database entry with better marketing.

That’s why @cancore_io is interesting. Do you know this project?

Since April, it’s facilitated $50M+ in volume, with ~760 trades a day, and tokenized assets on Canton settling against liquidity from public chains.

The signal isn’t how much value exists onchain.

It’s how much of that value actually moves.

Tokenized supply tells you what exists. Trading volume tells you what works. Do you agree?

tweets.text:
The hate in the comments is interesting.

I’m one of the only ones showing every buy and sell transparently, live, in a spreadsheet for my X subscribers.

No hiding. No cherry-picking.

2-month performance:

+45.26% 🟢
+$135,776.97 🟢

quote.text:
I sold my last Bitcoin at $85,000. Why?

There’s a lot of FOMO building on Twitter right now.

We accumulated around $58K–$62K, so after capturing that move, I’m taking profits.

That doesn’t mean I’m calling a local top. As described in my last post there is not a lot of sell pressure between this level and $88,000. 

It just means I’m managing the position based on the risk/reward in front of me.

And for the newer members:

Yes, I still expect a retrace toward the mid-$70Ks.

That remains my base thesis for now.

But I’m not going to force that thesis if the market starts telling us something different.

My invalidation is clear.

If Bitcoin starts closing multiple daily and weekly candles above $83K, I will consider the retracement thesis invalidated and reassess.

Simple.

I’m not emotionally attached to being right. I’m focused on responding to the data.

So for now, there is no reason for me to chase the market because Twitter is getting euphoric.

We already had our entries.

We already captured a significant move.

Now we wait.

The market doesn’t move in a straight line, and neither should your decision-making.

You want to have full insights in my buys and sells? 

Subscribe on X and get access to the live spreadsheet.

There’s a lot of FOMO building on Twitter right now.

We accumulated around $58K–$62K, so after capturing that move, I’m taking profits.

That doesn’t mean I’m calling a local top. As described in my last post there is not a lot of sell pressure between this level and $88,000. 

It just means I’m managing the position based on the risk/reward in front of me.

And for the newer members:

Yes, I still expect a retrace toward the mid-$70Ks.

That remains my base thesis for now.

My invalidation is clear.

Simple.

I’m not emotionally attached to being right. I’m focused on responding to the data.

So for now, there is no reason for me to chase the market because Twitter is getting euphoric.

We already had our entries.

We already captured a significant move.

Now we wait.

The market doesn’t move in a straight line, and neither should your decision-making.

tweets.text:
There's always a reason not to buy the bottom and always a reason not to sell the top. Some headline, some technical break, something that makes hesitation feel rational in the moment.

That doubt tends to show up exactly when conviction is hardest to hold, not randomly. Bottoms feel like they can always go lower, tops feel like they can always go higher.

That is how the psychology works in markets. It is good to be aware of this and check yourself from time to time.

Also important to make plans while the market is boring. Because when things get crazy, in either direction, it will be harder to make rational decisions.
